Title: Add New Product: Cost/Box is required by the backend but has no asterisk and no client-side validation - an empty value fails silently
Feature: Add New Product drawer > Cost/Box field
Description: Follow-up to BUG-PROD-001 (the disabled-field blocker is now fixed - Cost/Box is editable and a product can be created with a cost, including 0). Remaining gaps: (1) the backend still rejects a null Cost/Box ('Cost per box must not be null', HTTP 400), i.e. the field IS required, but its <label> has no 'ant-form-item-required' class so NO asterisk is shown (Product Name / Product Type / Company / Qty/Box / Retail Price/Box / Wholesale Price/Box all show one); (2) there is no client-side 'required' rule, so submitting with Cost/Box empty passes client validation, hits the server, gets a 400, and the UI shows NOTHING - no inline error, no red field, no persistent toast; the drawer just stays open. The user has no idea what is wrong.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; My Products > Add New Product open; every other required field filled with valid data; Cost/Box left blank.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open My Products > Add New Product. 2. Fill Product Name, Product Type, Company, Qty/Box, Retail Price/Box, Wholesale Price/Box. 3. Leave Cost/Box empty. 4. Click 'Confirm New Product'. 5. Observe: no asterisk on the Cost/Box label; on submit no inline error and no visible message; request body has costPerBox:null; response 400 'Cost per box must not be null'; drawer stays open.
Test Data: POST .../pharmacy-products/create/598 {..., costPerBox:null} -> 400 {"message":"Cost per box must not be null"}. With costPerBox:0 the same form -> 201 (product id 41006).
Expected Result: Since Cost/Box is mandatory: the label shows a red asterisk, and an empty submit is blocked client-side with an inline message such as 'Cost per box is required' (0 remains a valid value). If it is NOT meant to be mandatory, the backend should accept null / default it.
Actual Result: No asterisk; empty submit produces a silent 400 with no UI feedback.
Evidence: DOM: <label for="lastPurchasePricePerBox" class="" title="Cost/Box">Cost/Box</label> vs <label for="retailPricePerBox" class="ant-form-item-required" ...>; network create/598 costPerBox:null -> 400, costPerBox:0 -> 201
Remarks: Re-test 2026-09-09 07:28 UTC. Fix: add rules={[{ required: true, message: 'Cost per box is required' }]} to the Cost/Box Form.Item - AntD then renders the asterisk and blocks empty submit. Also map server-side field errors back to the field (ties in with BUG-PROD-003).

Title: My Products summary KPI cards (Total SKUs / Out of stock) do not refresh after a product is created or edited
Description: After creating a product from 'Add New Product', the table and the 'Total Products' counter update immediately, but the six summary cards above the filters (Total SKUs, Out of stock, Low stock, Expired, Expiring ≤90d, Stock value) do NOT - they keep their pre-create values until the page is reloaded. Observed on a full end-to-end create (product id 41007): 'Total Products' went 1 -> 2 and the new row appeared, but 'Total SKUs' stayed at 1 and 'Out of stock' stayed at 1; a hard reload then showed 2 / 2. The cards read from a separate summary endpoint that is not re-fetched on the create/edit success.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; My Products List open with the summary cards visible.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Note 'Total SKUs' and 'Out of stock'. 2. Create a product via 'Add New Product' (valid form). 3. Observe the new row + 'Total Products' increment, but the summary cards are unchanged. 4. Reload the page - the cards now update.
Test Data: Created 'QA FULL FLOW 260909' (id 41007); Total Products 1->2 but Total SKUs stayed 1 until reload.
Expected Result: The summary cards re-fetch (or are recomputed) when a product is created or edited, so they stay consistent with 'Total Products' and the table without a manual reload.
Actual Result: Summary cards are stale after create/edit; only a page reload refreshes them.
Evidence: post-create: Total Products=2, table shows 2 rows, but KPI 'Total SKUs'=1 / 'Out of stock'=1; after reload KPI=2 / 2
Remarks: Discovered 2026-09-09 during a full end-to-end creation check. Low severity (data is correct, only the summary widget lags) but confusing. Invalidate/refetch the summary query on the create/edit mutation success.

Title: A '%' character in any list-page search box crashes the page to a blank screen (URIError: URI malformed, no error boundary)
Feature: List-page search (Product Catalog, My Products - shared useQueryParams hook)
Description: Typing a '%' into a list search field (e.g. searching for the real catalog product '100%', or 'buy 50% off') puts the term into the URL query string; the app then re-reads its own query params and calls decodeURIComponent on a value it did not fully re-encode, which throws 'URIError: URI malformed' in normalizeQueryParams (src/utils/query-params.utils.ts:12) -> useQueryParams -> the page component (e.g. <ProductCatalog>) unmounts. There is NO error boundary, so the main content area goes completely BLANK - no table, no empty state, no error message. The only recovery is to edit the URL or navigate away. Confirmed on Product Catalog search and My Products search; every screen using useQueryParams is affected.
Preconditions: Any list screen with a search box (Product Catalog, My Products).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Product Catalog. 2. Type '50% off' (or '100%') into 'Search by name'. 3. Observe: URL becomes ...?productName=50%25+off, the console throws 'URIError: URI malformed' + 'An error occurred in the <ProductCatalog> component', and the page body renders blank. 4. Repeat on My Products (searchKey=...) - same blank crash.
Test Data: search terms: '100%', '50% off', any string containing '%'
Expected Result: The search term (incl. '%') is escaped once, sent to the API as a literal, and either returns matching rows or a normal empty state. A malformed query param must at worst be ignored, never crash the whole page; there should also be an error boundary.
Actual Result: decodeURIComponent throws, the list component unmounts, and the page is blank with no recovery.
Evidence: console: 'URIError: URI malformed at decodeURIComponent at normalizeQueryParams (src/utils/query-params.utils.ts:12) ... at ProductCatalog (src/features/product-catalog/ProductCatalogList.tsx:36)'; screenshots/catalog-percent-search-crash.png; URL ...?productName=50%25+off
Remarks: Discovered 2026-09-09. Two fixes needed: (1) encode/parse query params safely (guard decodeURIComponent in a try/catch and fall back to the raw string); (2) add a React error boundary around the routed page so a render error shows a retry, not a blank screen.

Title: Product Catalog per-row 'Import' button is not disabled during the request - rapid clicks fire N duplicate import calls
Description: Clicking a row's 'Import' button does not disable it (or show a spinner) while the import request is in flight, so a fast double/triple click sends that many POST .../pharmacy-products/import/<pid> requests for the same product. The backend is idempotent (dedups by product id, so only one product is created in My Products), so this is a cosmetic / efficiency issue rather than a data bug - but it is wasteful and the button should guard against it.
Preconditions: Product Catalog; a fresh (not-yet-imported) row.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Product Catalog. 2. Triple-click a row's 'Import' button quickly. 3. Observe 3 separate POST .../import/<pid> requests in DevTools Network; My Products still shows the product once.
Test Data: row '5-FLURIL 25 MG/ML 500 MG VIAL IV INJECTION' -> 3x POST import/598, 1 product in My Products
Expected Result: The button is disabled (or shows a loading state) on first click until the request resolves; at most one import request per click intent.
Actual Result: N clicks -> N import requests (net data still correct due to backend idempotency).
Evidence: network: 3x POST /api/1.0.0/secured/pharmacy-products/import/598 on a triple-click; My Products Total Products +1 only
Remarks: Discovered 2026-09-09. The bulk 'Import selected (N)' path is fine - it sends a single request for the whole batch.

Title: Wholesale Price/Box is enforced as mandatory on Add + Edit Product, but per requirement it must be optional
Feature: Add New Product / Edit Product drawer - Wholesale Price/Box field
Description: Requirement: 'Wholesale price/box' is OPTIONAL when adding a new product. Actual: it is required at every layer. (1) Add form: the label carries the 'ant-form-item-required' class so it shows a red asterisk; submitting with it empty (all other required fields valid) produces the inline error 'Wholesale price per box is required' and blocks the create - no product is made. (2) Backend: with client validation bypassed (the create request sent WITHOUT wholesalePricePerBox) the API returns 400 'Wholesale price per box must not be null'. (3) Edit form: the label is also required-marked; clearing Wholesale Price/Box and clicking 'Confirm Edit Product' shows the same inline error and blocks the save.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; My Products > Add New Product (and Edit Product on an existing product).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Add New Product. 2. Fill Product Name, Product Type, Company, Qty/Box, Cost/Box, Retail Price/Box. 3. Leave Wholesale Price/Box empty. 4. Click 'Confirm New Product'. 5. Observe the red asterisk on the label and the inline error 'Wholesale price per box is required'; drawer stays open; no product created. 6. (Backend) send the create request without wholesalePricePerBox -> 400 'Wholesale price per box must not be null'. 7. (Edit) open Edit on any product, clear Wholesale Price/Box, click 'Confirm Edit Product' -> same inline error, save blocked.
Test Data: form: Name QA WHOLESALE OPT 260909 / SYRUP / ACI LIMITED / 10 / cost 40 / retail 60 / wholesale <empty>. Backend probe: POST .../pharmacy-products/create/598 {..., no wholesalePricePerBox} -> 400.
Expected Result: Wholesale Price/Box has NO required asterisk; an empty value passes client validation; the create succeeds (201) with wholesale stored as null (or derived, e.g. = retail); Edit can also be saved without it.
Actual Result: Required asterisk shown; empty submit blocked client-side with 'Wholesale price per box is required'; backend rejects a null with 'Wholesale price per box must not be null'; Edit is blocked the same way.
Evidence: DOM: <label ... class="ant-form-item-required" title="Wholesale Price/Box">; inline '.ant-form-item-explain-error' = 'Wholesale price per box is required'; network create/598 without wholesalePricePerBox -> 400 {"message":"Wholesale price per box must not be null"}
Remarks: Verified 2026-09-09 10:2x UTC on pharmacy 598. Fix on both layers: drop the 'required' rule from the Wholesale Price/Box Form.Item (removes the asterisk + client block) AND make wholesalePricePerBox nullable on the create/update endpoints (or default it server-side, e.g. to retailPricePerBox). Applies to Edit Product too.

Title: Inventory Checkout discount is calculated against the FULL cart total, including products that have Free Qty (must be excluded)
Description: Per the Inventory Management spec (Free Qty & Discount rules), any product carrying Free Qty must be completely excluded from inventory-level discount distribution - the discount must be allocated only across eligible (non-free-qty) line items. On the live Inventory Checkout page, entering a percentage discount instead computes the amount against the ENTIRE cart total, including a line that has Free Qty, so that line wrongly absorbs a share of the discount.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Default mode; cart contains 2 items: TEST PRODUCT (Box Qty 3, BTP+VAT/Box Tk 7.20 -> Tk 21.60, Free Qty 5) and '100%' (Box Qty 2, BTP+VAT/Box Tk 105.00 -> Tk 210.00, Free Qty 0). Cart Total Price = Tk 231.60.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Build the cart described above (one line with Free Qty > 0, one line with Free Qty = 0). 2. Go to Inventory Checkout. 3. In 'Discount (on TP Price)', enter 10 with unit '%'. 4. Read 'Discount Amount' and 'Final Price'.
Test Data: 10% discount; eligible base should be only the '100%' line (Tk 210.00, since TEST PRODUCT has Free Qty 5)
Expected Result: Discount Amount = 10% of Tk 210.00 (eligible-only) = Tk 21.00; Final Price = Tk 231.60 - Tk 21.00 = Tk 210.60.
Actual Result: Discount Amount shown = Tk 23.16 (10% of the full Tk 231.60, i.e. the free-qty line was included); Final Price shown = Tk 208.44.
Evidence: screenshots/BUG-INV-001-discount-includes-free-qty.png
Remarks: The backend appears to compute the correct eligible-only final price when the record is actually saved (see BUG-INV-003/004) - so the bug is at minimum in the checkout page's LIVE preview calculation, and the mismatch between preview and saved record is a second, compounding defect.

Title: No 'Inventory Complete' success modal after checkout - spec-required summary/action modal is missing
Description: The functional spec requires that a successful 'Complete Inventory' action show an 'Inventory Complete' modal with Inventory ID, Inventory Details link, Supplier Information, Payment Status (Paid/Due), Inventory Type, Total Items, Total Price, Discount, Final Price, Total Paid, Due Amount, and Invoice / Hold List / New Inventory actions. The live app instead shows only a generic toast ('Created - Inventory has been created successfully') and silently redirects to the empty /inventory page.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; cart checked out with a valid supplier and payment.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Complete any inventory checkout (any mode). 2. Observe the result.
Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: An 'Inventory Complete' modal appears showing the transaction summary and Invoice / Hold List / New Inventory actions, per spec section 42.1.
Actual Result: Only a small toast notification appears; the user is dropped back on an empty Inventory page with no summary and no quick actions (must navigate to Inventory Record and open the row manually to see any detail).
Evidence: Toast text captured: 'Created / Inventory has been created successfully'; page navigates to https://pms-sql-portal.ems24.co/inventory
Remarks: This is a completeness gap against an explicit spec requirement, not a calculation defect.

Title: Checkout-time Final Price preview does not match the Final Price actually recorded - creates an unintended Due balance
Feature: Inventory Checkout - Paid to Supplier / Due
Description: At checkout, 'Paid to Supplier' auto-fills from the page's (incorrect, see BUG-INV-001) Final Price preview of Tk 208.44, and the user submits with that amount fully covering what the checkout page displays as the total. However the backend records the inventory with a different, and spec-correct, Final Price of Tk 210.60 (visible only afterwards in Inventory Record > Inventory Details). Because the amount actually paid (Tk 208.44) is less than the recorded Final Price (Tk 210.60), the completed inventory is left with an unintended Due of ~Tk 2 that the user never saw or agreed to at checkout time.
Preconditions: Same cart as BUG-INV-001 (one free-qty line, one eligible line), 10% discount applied, 'Paid to Supplier' left at its auto-filled value, checkout completed.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Reproduce BUG-INV-001's setup and apply the 10% discount. 2. Note the checkout page shows Final Price Tk 208.44 and auto-fills Paid = Tk 208.44 (Due Tk 0.00 on this page). 3. Select a supplier and click Complete Inventory. 4. Open Inventory Record and view the created record's 'Inventory Details'.
Test Data: Inventory #INV_20260914_02
Expected Result: The amount the user pays at checkout should equal the Final Price that is actually recorded, and Due should remain Tk 0.00 as shown at checkout time.
Actual Result: Inventory Details shows Total Price Tk 231.6, Final Price Tk 210.6, Total Paid Tk 208.44, Payment Status: Due (Due ~Tk 2), even though the checkout page had shown Due Tk 0.00 before submission.
Reproducibility: Always (whenever a cart with at least one free-qty and one eligible line receives a discount)
Evidence: screenshots/BUG-INV-003-checkout-vs-record-mismatch.png; Inventory Record list row shows Bill Amount 'Tk 210.6 -Tk 10 disc', Paid 'Tk 208.44', 'Due Tk 2'
Remarks: Direct consequence of BUG-INV-001; root cause is the checkout page's discount preview formula, not the backend persistence. Flagged Critical because it produces an incorrect supplier-due balance on a real financial transaction without any warning to the user.

Title: Line-item Purchase Price in Inventory Record does not reflect any allocated discount
Feature: Inventory Record - Inventory Details - Inventory Items table
Description: Per spec, unit Purchase Price = Unit TP/BTP+VAT - Unit Allocated Discount + Unit VAT, i.e. an eligible (non-free-qty) line's stored per-box purchase price should decrease once a discount is applied and allocated to it. In the created record, both line items' 'Purchase Price' are shown unchanged from their pre-discount BTP+VAT/Box values.
Preconditions: Same inventory as BUG-INV-001/003 (#INV_20260914_02), 10% discount applied.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Reproduce BUG-INV-001's checkout with 10% discount and complete the inventory. 2. Open Inventory Record > Inventory Details for the created record. 3. Inspect the 'Purchase Price' column for each line.
Test Data: TEST PRODUCT: pre-discount BTP+VAT/Box Tk 7.20; '100%': pre-discount BTP+VAT/Box Tk 105.00
Expected Result: The eligible line ('100%', no Free Qty) should show a reduced per-box Purchase Price reflecting its allocated share of the discount (e.g. ~Tk 94.50/box if the full Tk 21 discount is allocated to its 2 boxes); the free-qty line (TEST PRODUCT) should be unaffected.
Actual Result: Both lines show their original pre-discount per-box price (Tk 7.20 and Tk 105.00 respectively) with Total Price Tk 21.6 and Tk 210 - i.e. no discount is reflected at the line-item / costing level at all, even though the transaction-level Final Price does account for a discount.
Evidence: Inventory Details dialog for #INV_20260914_02: 'TEST PRODUCT ... Tk 7.2 Per box ... Tk 21.6' and '100% ... Tk 105 Per box ... Tk 210'
Remarks: Impacts downstream Avg Purchase Price / Stock Value reporting accuracy whenever a discount is used.

Title: Opening Stock mode: manually overriding BTP+VAT/Box does not back-calculate Opening Stock (%)
Feature: Inventory - Add Items to Cart (Opening Stock mode)
Description: The spec gives a concrete worked example: Retail price = 100, Box Qty = 10, user manually overrides BTP+VAT/Box to Tk 80 -> Total Tk 800, and Opening Stock (%) should then be recalculated to 20 (derived from the manual override). On the live page the Opening Stock (%) field stays at its prior value (12, the default) and is never updated after a manual BTP+VAT/Box override.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Opening Stock mode; product with Retail Price/Box = 100 selected; Box Qty = 10.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Switch Inventory Mode to Opening Stock. 2. Select TEST PRODUCT (Retail Price/Box auto-loads 100; Opening Stock (%) auto-loads 12). 3. Set Box Qty = 10. 4. Manually change BTP+VAT/Box to 80 and tab out. 5. Read the Opening Stock (%) field.
Test Data: Retail Price/Box 100, Box Qty 10, manual BTP+VAT/Box 80
Expected Result: Opening Stock (%) recalculates to 20, per spec section 19's worked example.
Actual Result: Opening Stock (%) remains 12; Total BTP + VAT does correctly update to 800 (80 x 10), but the percentage field is never touched.
Evidence: screenshots/BUG-INV-005-opening-stock-pct-not-recalculated.png
Remarks: Closed 2026-10-12 by the product owner: the Opening Stock (%) does NOT need to be back-calculated from a manual BTP+VAT/Box. Original observation (kept for history): The exact Retail-to-BTP formula for the initial 12% auto-calculation is itself an unconfirmed business rule per the spec (section 48) and was NOT asserted as a bug here - only the documented reverse-calculation behavior in section 19, which is unambiguous, was tested.

Title: Opening Stock mode: editing Retail Price/Box after a manual BTP+VAT/Box override silently discards the override
Feature: Inventory - Add Items to Cart (Opening Stock mode)
Description: Spec section 20 states that changing Retail Price/Box should trigger recalculation of BTP+VAT/Box only 'when the BTP value is still system-calculated rather than manually overridden' - i.e. once a user has manually entered BTP+VAT/Box, a later Retail Price edit must NOT overwrite it. On the live page, editing Retail Price/Box after a manual BTP+VAT/Box override recalculates and overwrites the manually entered value anyway.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Opening Stock mode; TEST PRODUCT selected, Box Qty 10, BTP+VAT/Box manually overridden to 80 (reproduces BUG-INV-005 first).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Reproduce BUG-INV-005 up to the manual BTP+VAT/Box = 80 override. 2. Change Retail Price/Box from 100 to 150 and tab out. 3. Read BTP+VAT/Box.
Test Data: Manual BTP+VAT/Box 80 -> Retail Price/Box changed to 150
Expected Result: BTP+VAT/Box remains 80 (the user's manual entry is preserved); only Retail Price/Box changes.
Actual Result: BTP+VAT/Box is silently recalculated to 132 (overwriting the user's manual entry of 80).
Evidence: Field trace: BTP+VAT/Box 80 (manual) -> Retail Price/Box changed 100->150 -> BTP+VAT/Box auto-changed to 132
Remarks: Closed 2026-10-12 by the product owner: re-deriving BTP+VAT/Box from Retail Price/Box after a manual override is acceptable behaviour. Original observation (kept for history): Real-world risk: a pharmacist who manually corrects a purchase cost and then tweaks the retail/selling price afterwards will have their cost entry silently discarded, without any indication in the UI.

Title: Inventory Record list 'Bill Amount' discount badge shows the raw entered discount rate, not the calculated discount amount
Feature: Inventory Record - list table - Bill Amount column
Description: On the Inventory Record list, the Bill Amount cell for a discounted inventory shows a small '-Tk N disc' badge. For the transaction created in BUG-INV-001 (10% discount, actual allocated discount ~Tk 21), the badge reads '-Tk 10 disc' - i.e. it appears to render the raw entered discount rate (10, as typed into the %/flat field) prefixed with 'Tk', rather than the computed discount amount, which is misleading when scanning the list.
Preconditions: An inventory record created with a percentage discount.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Complete an inventory checkout with a percentage discount (e.g. 10%). 2. Open Inventory Record and read the 'Bill Amount' cell for that row.
Test Data: 10% discount entered; backend-recorded discount ~Tk 21 (see BUG-INV-001/003)
Expected Result: The badge shows the actual discount amount (e.g. '-Tk 21 disc'), or otherwise clearly labels the value as a rate ('-10% disc') if that is what is intended.
Actual Result: Badge reads '-Tk 10 disc', which looks like a currency amount but is actually the entered percentage value with a 'Tk' prefix.
Evidence: Inventory Record row for #INV_20260914_02: 'Tk 210.6' / '-Tk 10 disc'
Remarks: Cosmetic/labeling defect, but compounds the confusion already caused by BUG-INV-001/003/004 when reconciling discount figures across the app. RECONFIRMED 2026-09-15 per user request to verify the Inventory Record table's discount display specifically for a genuine Percentage discount: #INV_20260915_21 (10% Percentage discount, Discount Amount Tk21.00) shows the identical badge pattern '-Tk 10 disc' - the raw entered rate (10) with a 'Tk' prefix, not the computed Tk21.00 amount and not labelled as a percentage. Confirms this bug reproduces consistently for the Percentage discount type, not just the case it was originally filed against.

Title: Inventory 'Bulk Import' button is completely non-functional
Description: The 'Bulk Import' button on the Inventory page (intended to let the user upload a supplier invoice and have it populate the cart, per the module's stated purpose in spec section 1) produces no visible or observable effect when clicked: no modal, no drawer, no native file-chooser dialog, no new network request, and no console error. Verified by inspecting the DOM for any input[type=file] element (none exists) and the network log (no new request fired) immediately after the click.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Inventory > Default mode (reproduced there; not mode-specific).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open /inventory. 2. Click 'Bulk Import'. 3. Observe the page - no modal/drawer/file picker appears. 4. Check the DOM for input[type=file] elements (none). 5. Check network requests fired after the click (none, beyond pre-existing page-load calls).
Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: Clicking 'Bulk Import' opens a file-upload modal/drawer allowing the user to select and upload an invoice file, which is then parsed to populate the Inventory Cart.
Actual Result: Nothing happens. The button receives focus (shows an 'active' state) but triggers no UI change, no file chooser, and no network activity whatsoever.
Evidence: screenshots/BUG-INV-008-bulk-import-dead.png; document.querySelectorAll('input[type=file]') -> []; browser_network_requests immediately after click shows no new request
Remarks: Blocks the entire invoice-driven bulk-entry workflow described in the spec's Purpose section; users must add every line manually.

Title: Negative Retail Price / Min Qty are accepted with no validation error, then silently reset to 0 on save
Feature: Inventory - Add Items to Cart panel (Default mode)
Description: Entering a negative value into Retail Price/Box or Min Qty (pcs) is accepted by the input with no client-side guard or error message, and the item can be added to the cart successfully with the negative value still showing in the form. However, re-opening that same cart line via Edit shows Retail Price/Box and Min Qty reset to 0 - not the negative value the user saw and submitted. There is no validation message at any point telling the user their negative value was rejected or altered.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Inventory > Default mode; a product selected in the Add Items to Cart panel.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Select a product. 2. Set Retail Price/Box = -50 and Min Qty (pcs) = -10 (both accepted with no error). 3. Set Box Qty=1, Batch No, click Add Items to Cart (item added successfully, Total Items +1). 4. Click the new row's Edit icon. 5. Read Retail Price/Box and Min Qty in the reopened form.
Test Data: Retail Price/Box=-50, Min Qty=-10 (product: TEST PRODUCT)
Expected Result: Per spec section 46 ('Negative price - should not be permitted', 'Min Qty - Cannot be negative'), the field should reject the negative value client-side with a clear inline message, OR if silently corrected, the user should be told so at entry time - not discover a silent 0 only by reopening Edit.
Actual Result: No validation error at any point. The negative value is accepted, shown in the field, and the item is added to the cart normally. On Edit, both fields read back as '0', not '-50'/'-10' - confirmed NOT a general edit-reload defect, since a parallel test with positive values (Retail Price/Box=77, Min Qty=25) round-tripped correctly through Edit.
Evidence: Field trace: entered -50/-10 -> accepted, item added -> Edit reopen shows retail='0', minQty='0'; control test with 77/25 correctly round-tripped as 77/25
Remarks: Not a data-integrity risk (the bad value does not persist as negative), but a validation-feedback gap: the user is never told their input was invalid or changed.

Title: Selecting Storage type 'WHS' disables the only text input, leaving no way to enter warehouse/storage information
Feature: Inventory - Add Items to Cart panel - Storage field
Description: Spec section 23 requires that for storage type 'WHS / Warehouse', the 'User can enter warehouse/storage information'. On the live page, selecting 'WHS' in the Storage type dropdown instead DISABLES the adjacent text input (which is labelled 'Rack no' and used for the Rack case) - there is no alternate field for warehouse information. The user therefore cannot enter ANY storage location detail when WHS is selected.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Inventory > Default mode; a product selected in the Add Items to Cart panel.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Select a product. 2. In the Storage field, open the type dropdown and select 'WHS'. 3. Observe the adjacent text input.
Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: With 'WHS' selected, a text input (or equivalent) should be enabled and available for the user to enter warehouse/storage information, per spec section 23.
Actual Result: The only text input (id=rackNo, labelled 'Rack no') becomes disabled when 'WHS' is selected, with no alternate input appearing. No way exists to record warehouse/storage info for a WHS-stored item.
Evidence: screenshots/BUG-INV-010-whs-disables-input.png; snapshot shows textbox "Rack no" [disabled] immediately after selecting WHS
Remarks: Closed as NOT A DEFECT - confirmed intentional by the product owner on 2026-10-08. A pharmacy has a single warehouse, so selecting WHS needs no location text and the field is disabled on purpose. Likely a copy/reuse bug: the Rack-only input was probably intended to be swapped for a WHS-specific field (or re-enabled generically) but was left disabled instead.

Title: Complete Inventory shows ZERO user-facing feedback when the backend rejects the transaction (e.g. duplicate barcode)
Description: When the backend rejects a Complete Inventory submission (observed 400 response: "Barcode 'KFP1200' is used by more than one item in this inventory." - a legitimate server-side duplicate-barcode validation, itself not a bug), the frontend shows absolutely no error to the user: no toast, no inline message, no alert. The page simply stays on /inventory-checkout with the same state as before the click, giving no indication the submission failed or why. Confirmed via DOM query for .ant-message-notice/.ant-notification-notice/[role=alert] immediately after the failed click and again after a 2s wait - zero matching elements both times.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Inventory Checkout with a cart whose backend validation will fail (e.g. two lines of the same product that both resolve to the same existing barcode, with no explicit barcode override on either line).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Add the same product to the cart twice without setting an explicit Barcode Value on either line (both inherit the product's existing barcode). 2. Go to Inventory Checkout, select a supplier. 3. Click Complete Inventory. 4. Observe: no toast/alert appears anywhere on the page, though the network tab shows a 400 response.
Test Data: Cart with 2x 'TEST PRODUCT 2' lines (shared barcode 'KFP1200'), no discount, supplier 'Tuhin'
Expected Result: A clear, user-friendly error message (toast or inline) explains the transaction could not be completed and, ideally, why (e.g. 'Duplicate barcode used by more than one item') - matching the general error-handling requirement that failures must never be silent.
Actual Result: POST /api/1.0.0/secured/inventories/create/598 returns 400 with a clear backend message, but nothing reaches the UI. The user is left with a page that looks unchanged and no explanation - they cannot tell whether the click registered, whether anything is wrong, or what to fix.
Reproducibility: Always (for any 400 from this endpoint, not just the duplicate-barcode case observed)
Evidence: screenshots/BUG-INV-011-no-error-feedback-on-checkout-failure.png; network response body: {"errors":["Invalid request error occurred."],"message":"Barcode 'KFP1200' is used by more than one item in this inventory.","status":"400 BAD_REQUEST"}
Remarks: Discovered incidentally while testing multi-product discount distribution (TC-INV-CO-006); the underlying backend validation (reject duplicate barcodes within one inventory) is correct and desirable - the bug is purely the frontend's total silence on failure. This is a general Complete-Inventory error-handling gap, not specific to the barcode case.

Title: Double-clicking 'Complete Inventory' creates TWO separate, fully paid duplicate inventory transactions
Description: The 'Complete Inventory' button has no client-side double-submit guard (not disabled on first click, no in-flight request lock). A rapid double-click fires TWO independent POST /inventories/create requests, and the backend accepts BOTH (201 each), creating two fully separate, fully paid inventory records for what the user intended as a single purchase. Confirmed via network log (two 201 responses to the same create endpoint) and via Inventory Record (two new rows, #INV_..._07 and #INV_..._08, created in the same minute, identical in every field: same supplier, same '1 item', same Tk 94.5 bill, same Tk 94.5 CASH paid, same 'Paid' status).
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Inventory Checkout with a valid cart and supplier selected, Complete Inventory enabled.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Build a cart with one item, go to Checkout, select a supplier. 2. Rapidly double-click 'Complete Inventory' (two click events fired back to back, e.g. via btn.click(); btn.click();). 3. Check Inventory Record.
Test Data: Cart: '100%' Box Qty=1, Tk 94.50, supplier 'Tuhin', CASH, no discount
Expected Result: Only ONE inventory transaction is created; the second click is ignored (button disabled during the in-flight request) or blocked server-side as a duplicate submission.
Actual Result: Both clicks succeeded independently (two 201 responses from /api/1.0.0/secured/inventories/create/598). Inventory Record shows two separate, identical, fully-paid transactions (#INV_20260915_07 and #INV_20260915_08) for a single user action - meaning stock was added twice and payment was recorded twice for one real purchase.
Evidence: screenshots/BUG-INV-012-duplicate-inventory-on-doubleclick.png; network log: 2x POST inventories/create/598 -> 201, 201; Inventory Record rows #INV_20260915_07 and #INV_20260915_08, both Tuhin/Purchase/1 item/Tk 94.5/Tk 94.5 CASH/Paid, both timestamped 01:01 pm
Remarks: Highest-severity finding in the Inventory module: directly corrupts stock quantities and financial/payment records from an ordinary, common user action (an impatient or accidental double-click), with no confirmation step or undo. Compounds with BUG-INV-011 (no error feedback) - even if the backend DID reject a duplicate, the user would not be told either way.

Title: Inventory Cart row Edit/Delete icons are not keyboard-accessible and have no accessible name
Description: The Edit and Delete action icons on each Inventory Cart row are plain <div> elements with a click handler and cursor:pointer styling, but no role="button", no aria-label (or any other accessible name source), and no tabindex. Per HTML/ARIA semantics a <div> with none of these is not part of the default keyboard tab order and is announced as generic, unlabelled content (or skipped entirely) by screen readers.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Inventory page with at least one item in the cart.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Add an item to the Inventory cart. 2. Inspect the row's action cell: document.querySelectorAll('td:last-child div[style*="cursor: pointer"]') for the Edit/Delete divs. 3. Check each for role/aria-label/tabindex attributes. 4. Attempt to reach either icon via Tab key alone from elsewhere on the page.
Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: Each action icon is either a real <button> or a <div role="button"> with a descriptive aria-label (e.g. 'Edit TEST PRODUCT batch QA123') and tabindex="0", so it is reachable via Tab and operable via Enter/Space, and announced meaningfully by assistive technology.
Actual Result: Both icons return {role: null, ariaLabel: null, tabIndex: null} - a keyboard-only user cannot Tab to either control at all, and a screen-reader user gets no indication of their purpose. Editing or deleting a cart line is only possible with a mouse.
Evidence: screenshots/BUG-INV-013-cart-actions-not-keyboard-accessible.png; DOM query result: [{role:null,ariaLabel:null,tabIndex:null,tag:'DIV'}, {role:null,ariaLabel:null,tabIndex:null,tag:'DIV'}]
Remarks: Same recurring pattern as BUG-A11Y-001 (Products module: pharmacy-card Enter/Space did not activate) - icon-only interactive controls across this app consistently skip standard button semantics. By contrast, the Product/Company/Storage selects ARE fully keyboard-operable (type-to-filter + arrow keys + Enter, verified working) and required fields correctly carry aria-required="true", so this is not a blanket accessibility failure, just this specific icon-button pattern.

Title: Inventory accepts an already-expired Expiry Date with zero warning at every stage
Feature: Add Items to Cart - Expiry Date validation
Description: The Expiry Date calendar picker on the Add Items to Cart panel does not disable or warn against dates earlier than today. A date already in the past (i.e. already expired relative to the current date) can be picked, added to the cart, carried through Inventory Checkout with no warning, and Complete Inventory succeeds - saving a newly-received purchase whose batch is already expired. This directly contradicts the functional spec's own validation checklist, which explicitly lists "Invalid expiry - Should not be accepted".
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Inventory page, Add Items to Cart panel open; system date 15 Sept 2026.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Add Items to Cart, select a product, set Box Qty. 2. Click the Expiry Date field to open the calendar - note dates before today (e.g. 1 Sept 2026, 14 days in the past) are NOT disabled/greyed out. 3. Select a past date (1 Sept 2026) and Add Items to Cart - no validation error, cart shows "1 Sept 2026" in Exp date column. 4. Go to Inventory Checkout - no warning shown. 5. Select a supplier and click Complete Inventory - transaction succeeds (#INV_20260915_12, Tk 104.49, Paid). 6. Open Expired Products - the newly-purchased batch (QA_EXP_ALREADY_PAST) immediately appears, labelled "Expired 14d ago".
Test Data: Product: TEST PRODUCT; Box Qty: 1; Batch No: QA_EXP_ALREADY_PAST; Expiry Date: 01 Sep, 2026 (14 days before the 15 Sept 2026 system date).
Expected Result: Per the spec's validation table ("Invalid expiry - Should not be accepted"), the calendar should disable dates before today, or at minimum the client/server should reject a past expiry date with a clear validation message before the item can be added to the cart or the purchase completed.
Actual Result: The past date is accepted silently at every stage - cart, checkout, and the completed Inventory Record - with no error, warning, or confirmation prompt anywhere. The pharmacy ends up having formally "received" and paid for stock that is already expired the moment it enters the system, and it is immediately surfaced in the Expired Products list with no traceability back to the fact it was never valid stock.
Evidence: screenshots/BUG-INV-014-past-expiry-date-accepted.png; Expired Products row: TEST PRODUCT / QA_EXP_ALREADY_PAST / Expired 14d ago / 1 Sept 2026; Inventory Record #INV_20260915_12.
Remarks: Closed as NOT A DEFECT - confirmed intentional by the product owner on 2026-10-08. Past Expiry Dates are allowed on purpose (e.g. receiving stock that is already near/past expiry). Financial/inventory-integrity concern distinct from BUG-INV-011 (missing error feedback on a rejected 400): here the backend does not even reject the request, it fully accepts an already-expired batch as valid new stock. Not yet verified whether the Sale module would allow dispensing against this batch (FEFO enforcement per spec section 25 is untested and out of scope for the Inventory module pass) - flagged as a follow-up risk, not confirmed.

Title: Inventory Details view shows only the combined Total Paid and a list of payment methods, never the amount paid via each individual method
Feature: Inventory Checkout / Inventory Record - multi-method payment display
Description: When a single inventory transaction is paid using more than one payment method (e.g. part BANK, part CASH), the backend correctly stores a separate payments[] entry with its own amount and method for each split (confirmed via the raw API response: {amount:2, paymentMethod:BANK} and {amount:1.33, paymentMethod:CASH}). However, neither the Inventory Record list's Paid Amount column nor the Inventory Details drawer shows these amounts individually - both only display the combined total (e.g. "Tk 3.33") followed by a list of method name tags ("BANK", "CASH") with no amount attached to either tag.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; an inventory transaction completed using 2+ payment methods with different amounts.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. At Inventory Checkout, add a second payment row via the "+" button. 2. Set method A (e.g. BANK) = Tk 2.00, method B (e.g. CASH) = Tk 1.33. 3. Complete the transaction. 4. Open Inventory Record and view the row's Paid Amount cell, then open the row's Inventory Details drawer.
Test Data: BANK: Tk 2.00, CASH: Tk 1.33 (Final Price Tk 3.33).
Expected Result: The user can see how much was paid via each method (e.g. "BANK: Tk 2.00, CASH: Tk 1.33"), not just the combined total and an undifferentiated list of method names - needed for accounting reconciliation (e.g. matching bank deposits).
Actual Result: Both the list column and the Details drawer show "Tk 3.33" with method tags "BANK" "CASH" underneath/beside it, with no way to tell which amount went to which method from the UI. The correct data exists in the API response (GET .../inventories/id/{id}/{pharmacyId} returns a full payments[] array with per-entry amount+method) - this is a UI display gap, not a data-loss issue.
Evidence: screenshots/inventory-record-split-payment-details.png; API response for inventory #25 (INV_20260915_13): payments:[{amount:2,paymentMethod:{name:"BANK"}},{amount:1.33,paymentMethod:{name:"CASH"}}], while the Details drawer only rendered "Total Paid BANK CASH Tk 3.33".
Remarks: Backend data integrity is fine (verified via direct API response inspection) - purely a frontend rendering gap in both the Inventory Record list and the Details drawer.

Title: Checkout summary panel keeps the "Due" label and shows a negative amount when Paid Amount exceeds Final Price, instead of switching to "Advance"
Description: Per spec: "If the payment exceeds the payable balance, the additional amount shall be recorded as Supplier Advance." The live Inventory Checkout summary panel (before Complete Inventory is clicked) never relabels its "Due" row to "Advance" - when Paid Amount > Final Price it simply shows "Due: Tk -50.00" (a negative Due) instead of "Advance: Tk 50.00". After the transaction is actually completed, the persisted Inventory Record list DOES correctly show "Status: Advance Tk 50" - so this is specifically a pre-submission checkout-preview labelling defect, not a data/calculation defect.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Inventory Checkout with a cart worth a known Final Price and a supplier selected.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Build a cart with Final Price Tk 100.00. 2. At Checkout, select a supplier. 3. Set Paid Amount to Tk 150.00 (Tk 50 more than Final Price). 4. Read the checkout summary panel's Due/Advance row before clicking Complete Inventory.
Test Data: Final Price: Tk 100.00, Paid Amount: Tk 150.00.
Expected Result: The summary row should relabel itself "Advance" and show a positive Tk 50.00 once Paid Amount exceeds Final Price, matching the post-completion Inventory Record behaviour ("Status: Advance Tk 50").
Actual Result: The row stayed labelled "Due" and showed "Tk -50.00" (a negative value) the entire time the checkout form was open. Only after Complete Inventory was clicked and the transaction saved did the correct "Advance" label appear, on the Inventory Record list.
Evidence:
Checkout summary innerText captured live: "...Total Paid
Tk 150.00
Due
Tk -50.00..." immediately before Complete Inventory; compare to the same transaction's Inventory Record row afterward showing "Status: Advance Tk 50".
Remarks: Cosmetic/UX defect only - the underlying Paid/Due/Advance calculation and persistence are both correct (verified: supplier balance moved from Due Tk 50.52 to Due Tk 0.52, exactly netting the Tk 50 advance). A user reading the live checkout screen before submitting could be confused by a negative Due instead of a positive Advance.

Title: Inventory Details view (post-completion) omits most Pricing Breakdown and Inventory Items fields that the backend already returns
Description: The 'Inventory Details' drawer (opened via the eye/View Details icon from Inventory Record) renders only a small subset of the data the backend API already returns for the transaction. Pricing Breakdown shows only Total Items, Total Price, Final Price, Total Paid, and Payment Status - it omits Total TP Price, VAT Amount, and Discount Amount (on TP Price), even though these are all present in the checkout preview shown moments earlier and in the raw API response (totalTpPrice, vatAmount, discountAmount fields). The Inventory Items table shows only Details, Batch/Expiry, Rack No, Qty, Purchase Price, and Total Price - it omits Qty/Box, Min. Qty, Free, BTP+VAT, Discount, Retail Price, Whole Sale Price, and Barcode, even though every one of these values is present and correct in the item's API record (quantityInBox, minQty, freeQty, btpVatPerBox, retailPricePerBox, wholesalePricePerBox, barcodeValue).
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; a completed inventory transaction with a discount applied and all optional item fields (Min Qty, Retail/Wholesale Price, Barcode, Rack) populated.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create an inventory transaction (Default mode) for TEST PRODUCT: Box Qty 2, BTP+VAT/Box 100, Retail Price/Box 150, Wholesale Price/Box 130, Min Qty 25, Rack A1, Batch QA_DETAILVIEW_001, Barcode QA9988776655. 2. At Checkout apply a 10% discount and complete. 3. Open Inventory Record and click the eye icon to view Inventory Details. 4. Compare the rendered fields against the raw API response for the same inventory (GET .../inventories/id/{id}/{pharmacyId}).
Test Data: Box Qty 2, BTP+VAT/Box Tk 100, Retail Price/Box Tk 150, Wholesale Price/Box Tk 130, Min Qty 25, Discount 10%.
Expected Result: Per the required Inventory Details layout (reference screenshot supplied by stakeholder), the Pricing Breakdown section should show Total Items, Total Price, Total TP Price, VAT Amount, Discount Amount (on TP Price), Final Price, Total Paid, and Payment Status; the Inventory Items table should show Details, Batch/Expiry, Rack/Storage, Qty, Qty/Box, Min. Qty, Free, BTP+VAT, Discount, Total Price, Purchase Price, Retail Price, Whole Sale Price, and Barcode.
Actual Result: Pricing Breakdown showed only 5 of 8 required rows (missing Total TP Price, VAT Amount, Discount Amount). The Inventory Items table showed only 6 of 14 required columns (missing Qty/Box, Min. Qty, Free, BTP+VAT, Discount, Retail Price, Whole Sale Price, Barcode) - even though the backend API response for this exact inventory confirmed quantityInBox:10, minQty:25, freeQty:0, btpVatPerBox:100, retailPricePerBox:150, wholesalePricePerBox:130, barcodeValue:'QA9988776655' were all correctly stored.
Evidence: screenshots/inventory-details-view-strict-check.png; raw API response for inventory id 29 (INV_20260915_17) showing totalTpPrice:200.00, vatAmount:0.00, discountAmount:20.00, and item fields quantityInBox:10, minQty:25, retailPricePerBox:150, wholesalePricePerBox:130, barcodeValue:'QA9988776655' - none of which render in the Details drawer.
Remarks: Also confirms the pre-existing BUG-INV-004 (line-item Purchase Price/Total Price shown in this view never reflect allocated discount - both still show the pre-discount BTP+VAT values, Tk 100/box and Tk 200 total, instead of the backend's true post-discount purchasePrice of Tk 9.00/pc = Tk 90/box). Backend data integrity is fine throughout - this is purely a frontend rendering gap in the Details drawer, directly limiting the 'Inventory History Verification' capability required by spec section 44. RETESTED 2026-09-15 per user request with a genuine Percentage discount (checkout: TEST PRODUCT Tk100/box + TEST PRODUCT 2 Tk110/box, 10% discount, Discount Amount correctly computed as Tk21.00 = 10% of Tk210 Total Price; #INV_20260915_21, id 33): the Discount column is confirmed still entirely absent from the Inventory Items table for the Percentage case too (same 6-of-14 columns as before). Crucially, the raw API response (GET .../inventories/id/33/598) shows the backend stores discount ONLY at the inventory/header level (discountAmount:21.00, discountType:'PERCENTAGE', discountValue:10) - neither item object in the items[] array carries any per-item discount field at all (no discount amount, percent, or value; each item's totalItemPrice is the pre-discount value, 100.00 and 110.00, summing to totalPrice 210.00 rather than finalPrice 189.00). So this is not only a frontend rendering gap: the backend itself never computes or persists a per-product discount allocation, for either Discount Type. Confirms this ties directly to the user's original question (proportional-by-purchase-price allocation, always displayed as %, per spec section 39/48) - that allocation is not implemented anywhere yet, front or back end, so it cannot currently be verified as correct or incorrect; the column must first be added end-to-end before that check is possible.

Title: 'Required OTP Verification via SMS' on Add New Supplier Payment is not actually enforced - a payment is accepted with the toggle left 'Not verified'
Description: The 'Add New Supplier Payment' dialog (opened via Inventory Record's row kebab menu > Pay Due, or Supplier List's payment icon) displays a labelled control 'Required OTP Verification via SMS' with a toggle that starts in the 'Not verified' state. The word 'Required' implies this step is mandatory before a payment can be submitted. In practice, the 'Confirm New Payment' button is never disabled by this state, and clicking it submits the payment successfully with no OTP ever requested, sent, or entered.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; a supplier with an outstanding Due balance.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. From Inventory Record, open the kebab menu on any row for a supplier with a Due balance and select 'Pay Due' (or use Supplier List's payment icon). 2. Enter a Payment Amount and select a Payment Method. 3. Leave the 'Required OTP Verification via SMS' toggle in its default 'Not verified' state (do not request or enter any OTP). 4. Click 'Confirm New Payment'.
Test Data: Supplier: Tuhin, Payment Amount: Tk 0.52, Method: CASH.
Expected Result: Given the control is explicitly labelled 'Required', the system should block submission (disable Confirm, or reject the request server-side) until OTP verification is completed.
Actual Result: The 'Confirm New Payment' button remained enabled with the toggle still 'Not verified', and clicking it returned 201 Created (POST .../supplier-payments/create/1/598) - the payment was recorded successfully and the supplier's balance was updated (Due Tk 0.52 -> Tk 0.00), with no OTP step ever occurring.
Evidence: Network log: POST https://pms-sql-api.ems24.co/api/1.0.0/secured/supplier-payments/create/1/598 => 201, response body {"amount":0.52,...,"supplierBalance":0.00,...} with the OTP toggle never touched; Supplier List confirmed balance dropped to Tk 0 immediately after.
Remarks: Either the 'Required' OTP step is a planned-but-unimplemented control (dead UI), or it is meant to be optional and mislabelled. Either way, a control visually presented as a mandatory security/verification gate for a financial transaction currently provides no protection at all - worth flagging to the product owner regardless of which reading is correct.

Title: Cart and Checkout tables round a fractional Box Qty up to a whole number (0.5 displays as '1') while the underlying value and all money calculations stay correct
Feature: Inventory Cart / Inventory Checkout - Box Qty column display
Description: When Total Qty is manually overridden to a value that does not divide evenly by Qty/Box (per spec section 5.3), the Add Items to Cart panel correctly computes and shows the fractional Box Qty (e.g. 0.5). Once the line is added to the cart, however, the Cart table's 'Box Qty' column and the Checkout page's 'Box Qty' column both display the fractional value rounded up to the nearest whole box (e.g. '1' instead of '0.5'), even though the row's 'Total Price' column, the checkout summary totals, and the eventual saved record all continue to use the correct fractional value throughout.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; Default Inventory Mode; a product whose Qty/Box does not evenly divide the desired Total Qty (e.g. TEST PRODUCT 2, Qty/Box=10).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Select TEST PRODUCT 2 (Qty/Box=10) in Add Items to Cart. 2. Set Total Qty = 5 (does not divide evenly by 10) - the Box Qty field correctly shows 0.5 and Total BTP+VAT correctly recalculates to BTP+VAT/Box x 0.5. 3. Add to cart and read the Cart table's Box Qty column for that row. 4. Go to Inventory Checkout and read the Box Qty column there too. 5. Complete the transaction and compare against the raw API response and the post-completion Inventory Details view.
Test Data: Product: TEST PRODUCT 2 (Qty/Box=10, BTP+VAT/Box=Tk 110). Total Qty entered: 5 (expected Box Qty = 0.5).
Expected Result: The Cart table and Checkout table's Box Qty column should show '0.5' (matching the Add Items panel, the Inventory Details view shown after completion, and the raw API's boxQty:0.5), not a value rounded to a whole box.
Actual Result: Both the Cart table and the Checkout table displayed Box Qty as '1' for this line, while the same row's Total Price column correctly showed 'Tk 55.00' (= 0.5 x Tk 110, not 1 x Tk 110 = Tk 110). After completing the transaction, the raw API response confirmed items[0].boxQty:0.5 and totalQty:5 were stored correctly, and the post-completion Inventory Details view's Qty column correctly rendered '0.5box 5pc' - so the defect is isolated entirely to the Cart and Checkout tables' Box Qty column rendering; no other screen, and no money calculation anywhere, is affected.
Evidence: Cart table row: Box Qty='1', BTP+VAT='Tk 110.00', Total Price='Tk 55.00'. Checkout table row: identical. Checkout summary: Total Price/Final Price both 'Tk 55.00'. Raw API response for inventory id 32 (INV_20260915_20): items[0].boxQty:0.5, totalQty:5, totalItemPrice:55.00. Inventory Details view Qty cell: '0.5box5pc'.
Remarks: Reported directly by the user. A pharmacy staff member reading the Cart or Checkout screen would reasonably believe a full extra box (1) is being received/charged instead of half a box (0.5), even though they would actually be charged/receive the correct fractional amount - a real (if narrow) risk of user confusion about physical stock being received, despite the money being correct. This also ties into the still-open spec ambiguity in section 48 ('Total Qty override - what happens when Total Qty / Qty/Box produces a fractional Box Qty') - fractional Box Qty is clearly being accepted and correctly priced, so if fractional boxes are not meant to be allowed at all, the right fix may be validation at entry time rather than a display rounding fix.

Title: Flat (Tk) discount at Checkout makes Complete Inventory fail silently - backend rejects the request (400: invalid discountType), but the user sees nothing
Description: Spec section 37 explicitly requires Checkout to support two discount types: Percentage and Flat. Switching the discount unit dropdown from '%' to 'Tk' and entering an amount works correctly on-screen (Discount Amount, Final Price, Total Paid all recalculate correctly and stay flat - i.e. do not change proportionally - when the cart total changes, proving the UI genuinely treats it as a flat amount). However, clicking Complete Inventory with a Flat discount active causes the backend to reject the request outright, and the checkout screen shows absolutely no error, toast, or any other indication that anything went wrong - the page simply stays exactly as it was, with Complete Inventory still enabled, as if nothing had been clicked.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; a cart with at least one item, at Inventory Checkout.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Build a cart (e.g. TEST PRODUCT Tk100 + TEST PRODUCT 2 Tk110 = Total Price Tk210). 2. At Checkout, change the discount unit dropdown from '%' to 'Tk'. 3. Enter a discount amount, e.g. 15 (Discount Amount correctly shows Tk15.00, Final Price Tk195.00 - confirmed NOT recalculated as a percentage when the cart total changed from Tk100 to Tk210, proving the flat-amount UI logic itself is correct). 4. Select a supplier. 5. Click Complete Inventory. 6. Observe the page - no visible change, no error message. 7. Inspect the network tab / console for the POST to .../inventories/create/{pharmacyId}.
Test Data: Cart: TEST PRODUCT (Tk100) + TEST PRODUCT 2 (Tk110) = Tk210 Total Price. Discount: Tk 15 Flat. Supplier: Tuhin.
Expected Result: Per spec section 37, a Flat discount is an explicitly supported, first-class discount type - Complete Inventory should succeed exactly as it does for a Percentage discount, creating the inventory record with the flat discount correctly applied and stored.
Actual Result: The POST to /api/1.0.0/secured/inventories/create/598 returned 400 Bad Request with body: {"errors":["Request Body is missing"],"message":"Invalid value for field 'discountType': expected a value of type InventoryDiscountType."}. The actual request payload sent "discountType":"FLAT" - the backend's InventoryDiscountType enum apparently does not accept the literal string "FLAT" that the frontend sends (by contrast, a Percentage discount correctly sends "discountType":"PERCENTAGE", which the backend does accept, per prior successful transactions). No inventory record was created, and the checkout page showed zero visible indication of the failure - no toast, no inline error, no disabled/loading state resolution - Complete Inventory simply appeared to do nothing.
Evidence: Console error: 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400 () @ .../inventories/create/598'. Request body confirmed discountType:"FLAT". Response body: {"message":"Invalid value for field 'discountType': expected a value of type InventoryDiscountType."}. Screenshot screenshots/flat-discount-checkout-silent-failure.png taken immediately after clicking Complete Inventory shows the checkout form completely unchanged, no error visible anywhere.
Remarks: This is a frontend/backend contract mismatch (the frontend's literal string for the Flat discount type does not match what the backend's enum accepts) combined with the recurring silent-failure UX pattern already flagged in BUG-INV-011 (Complete Inventory gives zero feedback on any backend rejection). Because Flat discount can never be successfully saved in the current build, the user-reported symptom of the Inventory Details drawer 'always showing % even when Flat was selected at checkout' could not be independently reproduced or confirmed at first. User has since CONFIRMED this is intended, correct behaviour by design (2026-09-15, also added to spec section 39): a Flat discount is meant to distribute across eligible products proportionally by purchase price - the same basis already used for a Percentage discount - and each product's resulting allocated share is ALWAYS meant to display as a percentage on Inventory Details regardless of which Discount Type was entered at checkout. So once BUG-INV-020 itself is fixed (Flat discount can actually be saved), the '%' display per product is NOT something to flag as a defect - it should be re-verified only for correctness of the computed percentage (i.e. each product's % = its allocated discount / its own purchase price), not for using % as the unit.

Title: Per-product discount allocation (spec section 39/44.1) is not implemented anywhere - neither the backend nor the Inventory Details drawer ever compute, persist, or display a discounted product's proportional share
Feature: Inventory Checkout (Percentage discount) - Inventory Record - Inventory Details drawer
Description: Per spec section 39 'Discount Distribution' and section 44.1 'Inventory Details View - Required Fields', when a discount is applied at Checkout, each eligible product's allocated share must be computed proportionally to its purchase price and always shown as a percentage (%) on the Inventory Details drawer's per-item 'Discount' column - regardless of whether Percentage or Flat was entered at checkout. Tested with a genuine Percentage discount (the case that unambiguously should work, since the checkout math itself distributes cleanly - 10% of a total equals the sum of 10% of each part). Confirmed the feature does not exist at all: the Inventory Details drawer's Items table has no Discount column (ties to BUG-INV-017), and - going deeper via the raw API - the backend itself never computes or stores any per-item discount value. The completed inventory's discount is recorded ONLY at the header/inventory level (discountAmount, discountType, discountValue); every item record in items[] is missing any discount-related field whatsoever, and each item's totalItemPrice is the pre-discount value.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma; a cart of 2+ distinguishable-price products, at Inventory Checkout.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Build a cart: TEST PRODUCT Tk100/box + TEST PRODUCT 2 Tk110/box (Total Price Tk210, prices deliberately distinguishable so a % vs Flat miscalculation would be visible). 2. At Checkout, apply a genuine 10% Percentage discount (confirm Discount Amount computes to Tk21.00 = 10% of Tk210, and the unit selector genuinely reads '%'). 3. Complete the inventory (#INV_20260915_21, backend id 33). 4. Open Inventory Record and click the eye/View Details icon. 5. Inspect the Inventory Items table for a per-product Discount value. 6. Cross-reference the raw API response GET .../inventories/id/33/598.
Test Data: Cart: TEST PRODUCT (Tk100/box) + TEST PRODUCT 2 (Tk110/box) = Tk210 Total Price. Discount: 10% Percentage (Discount Amount Tk21.00, Final Price Tk189.00). Supplier: Tuhin.
Expected Result: Per spec section 39/44.1: each eligible product's allocated discount share is computed proportionally to its purchase price (for this cart, both items are eligible and would receive exactly 10% each, since 10% of the whole equals 10% of every part), persisted with the item record, and displayed as a % in the Inventory Details drawer's Discount column for that product.
Actual Result: The Inventory Details drawer's Items table has no Discount column at all (6 of 14 required columns render, same gap as BUG-INV-017). Raw API response for inventory id 33 confirms the backend never computes this either: discountAmount:21.00, discountType:'PERCENTAGE', discountValue:10 are present only at the top level of the response; neither item object in items[] (id 45 'TEST PRODUCT', id 46 'TEST PRODUCT 2') has ANY discount-related key - no discountAmount, discountPercent, discountValue, or equivalent. Each item's totalItemPrice is the pre-discount amount (100.00 and 110.00), summing to totalPrice (210.00) rather than finalPrice (189.00).
Evidence: Raw API response for inventory id 33 (INV_20260915_21): header discountAmount:21.00/discountType:'PERCENTAGE'/discountValue:10; items[0] and items[1] both missing every discount-related key, totalItemPrice 100.00/110.00 each pre-discount. Live pytest run (tests/inventory/test_inventory_record.py::TestPerProductDiscountAllocation) reproduced the identical pattern independently via automation.
Remarks: Distinct root cause from BUG-INV-017: BUG-INV-017 is about the frontend failing to render fields the backend DOES already return; this is about a feature (proportional per-product discount allocation) that does not exist anywhere in the stack yet, front or back end - there is currently no data for any UI column to render, even a fixed one. This directly answers the user's original question (whether the Details drawer wrongly shows % for a Flat-entered discount): it cannot yet be answered either way, because no per-product discount of any kind - % or Tk - is ever computed or shown for ANY discount type, including the straightforward Percentage case tested here. Fixing this requires (1) the backend to compute and persist each item's proportional discount share on save, and (2) the Inventory Details drawer to add the missing Discount column (BUG-INV-017) and render that value as a %, per spec section 39/44.1.

Title: Inventory Return / Stock Adjustment Details view renders broken line-item data: Qty shows 0, Purchase Price shows Tk0, Rack No shows storage type, Payment Status contradicts Total Paid
Feature: Inventory Return Details drawer; Stock Adjust Details drawer
Description: Both the Inventory Return Details view (opened from Inventory Return Record) and the Stock Adjustment Details view (opened from Stock Adjust Record) share the same broken rendering for completed transaction line items: (1) the Qty column shows '0 box / 0 pc' even though the transaction genuinely moved a non-zero quantity (raw API confirms items[].boxQty and items[].quantityInBox/returnedQty are 0 while items[].totalQty correctly holds the real value); (2) Purchase Price shows 'Tk 0 Per box' even though items[].purchasePrice is correctly populated in the API (the UI reads box-level fields like btpVatPerBox which are null for these transaction types, instead of falling back to purchasePrice); (3) Rack No shows the storage TYPE ('Warehouse') instead of the batch's real rack identifier (item-level rackNo is null; pharmacyProduct.rackNo, e.g. '1', is never used as a fallback); (4) Payment Status shows 'Paid' while the same panel's Total Paid shows 'Tk 0' - a direct on-screen contradiction, because these transaction types have no actual payment concept but reuse the Inventory Purchase payment-status model verbatim.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma (598); a completed Inventory Return or Stock Adjustment transaction against a batch that has a real Rack No, Qty and Purchase Price.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Complete a partial return or stock adjustment of a known batch (e.g. 15 pc of TEST PRODUCT, Rack 1, Tk8/pc purchase price). 2. Open Inventory Return Record (or Stock Adjust Record) and click View Details. 3. Compare the Inventory Items table's Qty/Purchase Price/Rack No columns and the Pricing Breakdown's Payment Status/Total Paid against the raw API response for the same transaction (GET .../inventories/id/{id}/598).
Test Data: Inventory Return #INV_20260916_04 (id 6): 15 pc returned, Rack 1, Tk8.00/pc. Stock Adjustment #INV_20260916_05 (id 7): 10 pc Missing, Rack 1, Tk8.00/pc.
Expected Result: Qty shows the real returned/adjusted quantity (e.g. 15 pc / 10 pc); Purchase Price shows the real per-unit or per-box price (Tk8.00/pc or Tk80.00/box); Rack No shows '1'; Payment Status is consistent with Total Paid (a Tk0-paid transaction should not read 'Paid').
Actual Result: Return id 6: items[0] = {boxQty:0, returnedQty:0, totalQty:15, purchasePrice:8.0000, rackNo:null, storageType:'WAREHOUSE'}; UI showed Qty '0 box / 0 pc', Purchase Price 'Tk 0 Per box', Rack No 'Warehouse'. Header: paymentStatus:'PAID', paidAmount:0; UI showed Payment Status 'Paid' beside Total Paid 'Tk 0'. Stock Adjustment id 7 reproduces the identical pattern: items[0] = {boxQty:0, quantityInBox:0, totalQty:10, purchasePrice:8.0000, rackNo:null, storageType:'WAREHOUSE'}; batchNo additionally null (see BUG-INV-023); paymentStatus:'PAID', paidAmount:0 again contradicts Total Paid 'Tk 0' on screen.
Evidence: Raw API GET .../inventories/id/6/598 and GET .../inventories/id/7/598, both captured via browser_network_request; screenshots of both Details drawers alongside the API JSON.
Remarks: One shared root cause across two transaction types (Return, Stock Adjustment) - filed as a single bug rather than duplicated per module. Distinct from the pre-existing BUG-INV-017 (Inventory PURCHASE Details missing columns) - this is a different transaction type's Details view rendering data as zero/wrong even where the API has it.

Title: Stock Adjustment never persists the Batch No of the adjusted batch (items[].batchNo is always null)
Description: Spec explicitly requires: 'The Stock Adjustment record shall retain the product, batch, quantity, purchase price, total loss amount, and adjustment type.' The completed Stock Adjustment's line item never records which batch was adjusted - items[].batchNo is null in the raw API response even though the adjustment was made against an unambiguous, named batch (BATCH_20260916_02). This is worse than Inventory Return, whose completed items DO retain batchNo correctly. Consequently the Stock Adjust Record / Details view's Batch/Expiry column renders completely blank, and there is no way to audit which physical batch a loss was recorded against.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma (598); a batch with a known Batch No and available quantity.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open /stock-adjust. 2. Select a product and a named batch (e.g. BATCH_20260916_02). 3. Enter an Adjust Qty and add to cart. 4. Complete the Stock Adjust (type Missing). 5. Inspect the raw API response for the created record (GET .../inventories/id/{id}/598) and the Stock Adjust Record Details drawer's Batch/Expiry column.
Test Data: TEST PRODUCT, BATCH_20260916_02, 10 pc Missing adjustment, #INV_20260916_05 (id 7).
Expected Result: items[0].batchNo equals 'BATCH_20260916_02'; the Details drawer's Batch/Expiry column shows 'BATCH_20260916_02'.
Actual Result: items[0].batchNo is null in the raw API response; the Details drawer's Batch/Expiry column is completely empty (blank) for this line.
Evidence: Raw API GET .../inventories/id/7/598: items[0].batchNo == null.
Remarks: A genuine backend data-loss defect, not merely a frontend rendering gap - the batch identity is unrecoverable from this record once created, undermining traceability for loss/audit purposes (compare spec's general emphasis on complete inventory history).

Title: Completed Stock Adjustments never update the Dashboard's Business Loss / Stock Write-off figure
Feature: Stock Adjust Checkout > Complete Stock Adjust; Dashboard > Cashbook widget
Description: Spec states explicitly: 'The corresponding inventory value shall be reduced from the Inventory Balance. The same amount shall be recorded as a Business Loss. In summary: Stock Adjustment Amount = Inventory Value Reduction = Business Loss.' The stock-quantity side of this works correctly (verified: pharmacyProduct.quantity dropped from 100 to 90 after a 10 pc Missing adjustment), but the financial Business Loss bookkeeping never appears anywhere: the Dashboard's Cashbook widget has a labelled 'Stock Write-off' line that remained 'Tk 0' both before and after completing a Tk80 Missing adjustment, even after a full page reload/re-navigation.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma (598); Dashboard's Cashbook widget visible; a product with an adjustable batch.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open /dashboard and note the Cashbook widget's 'Stock Write-off' value. 2. Complete a Missing (or Destroyed) Stock Adjustment for a known Tk amount (e.g. Tk80). 3. Navigate back to /dashboard (fresh navigation, not just a soft refresh). 4. Re-read 'Stock Write-off'.
Test Data: 10 pc Missing adjustment of TEST PRODUCT, Final Price Tk80.00, #INV_20260916_05.
Expected Result: 'Stock Write-off' increases by Tk80.00 (or by the adjustment's Final Price), and the dashboard's Net calculation reflects the loss.
Actual Result: 'Stock Write-off' remained 'Tk 0' after the completed Tk80 adjustment, both immediately and after a fresh navigation to /dashboard.
Evidence: Dashboard screenshot before/after showing 'Stock Write-off: Tk 0' unchanged; Stock Adjust Record confirming the Tk80 Missing adjustment completed successfully (#INV_20260916_05, status Paid, Bill Amount Tk80). Also checked Accounting > Expenses (Expense List) after the Tk80 Missing adjustment: 'Total Expenses (0) / No expense found' - the loss does not appear there either, so there is currently NO location anywhere in the app's reporting where a completed Stock Adjustment's loss amount is ever recorded.
Remarks: Critical severity because this breaks the core financial-integrity guarantee the spec explicitly calls out in its own worked equation (Stock Adjustment Amount = Inventory Value Reduction = Business Loss) - a pharmacy owner has no way to see their true business loss from missing/destroyed stock anywhere in the reporting surfaced today.

Title: Stock Adjust Checkout shows a Demurrage line item, contradicting the spec's explicit 'no Demurrage for Stock Adjustment' rule
Description: Spec states: 'Unlike Inventory Return: There shall be no Demurrage.' The Stock Adjust Checkout drawer's pricing summary nonetheless includes a 'Demurrage Amount (0%): Tk 0.00' line, apparently because the Inventory Return checkout's pricing-breakdown component was reused verbatim for Stock Adjustment without removing the Demurrage row. There is no input to set a non-zero demurrage in this drawer (unlike Return's genuine Demurrage input), so the value is always 0 and has no functional/financial impact - but its mere presence contradicts the spec and could confuse users. Separately, the Adjustment Type field (Missing/Destroyed) is labelled 'Inventory type' on screen, reusing Inventory Checkout's copy instead of the spec's own term 'Adjustment Type' - a minor, related labelling inconsistency in the same reused-component pattern.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma (598); an item added to the Stock Adjust cart.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open /stock-adjust, add an item to the cart. 2. Click Go to Stock Adjust Checkout. 3. Read the pricing summary panel.
Test Data: 10 pc Missing adjustment, Tk80.00 total.
Expected Result: The Stock Adjust Checkout pricing summary shows only Total Items / Total Adjust Price / Final Price (Stock Adjustment) - no Demurrage line, per spec.
Actual Result: Summary showed: Total Items 10, Total Adjust Price Tk80.00, 'Demurrage Amount (0%): Tk 0.00', Final Price (Stock Adjustment) Tk80.00.
Evidence: Screenshot of Stock Adjust Checkout drawer showing the Demurrage Amount (0%) line.
Remarks: Low severity/cosmetic since the value is inert (always Tk0, no input), but a straightforward spec-conformance defect and an easy fix (remove the reused Demurrage row for this checkout variant; relabel 'Inventory type' to 'Adjustment Type').

Title: Cancel Return confirmation popover renders entirely outside the visible viewport, making the Cancel Return feature unusable via mouse
Feature: Inventory Return Record > row kebab menu > Cancel Return
Description: Spec requires: 'The user shall also be able to Cancel a Return.' Clicking 'Cancel Return' in a row's kebab menu correctly opens an AntD Popconfirm ('Cancel this return? It will be marked cancelled and left out of future totals. Keep it / Yes, cancel it'), but at the default 1920px viewport width this Popconfirm is positioned entirely off-screen to the right (measured via getBoundingClientRect at x=1952.9, while window.innerWidth=1920 and document.documentElement.scrollWidth=2328 with scrollX=0). The element exists in the DOM/accessibility tree (confirmed clickable via direct ref/automation) but is never visible or reachable by a real mouse user in the default layout, since there is no visible horizontal-scroll affordance hinting that content is cut off. This effectively blocks the documented Cancel Return feature for any row whose kebab trigger sits near the table's right edge - which, given the Action column is the last column, is every row.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma (598); Inventory Return Record has at least one row; viewport at or near 1920px width (a common desktop default).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open /inventory-return-record at default viewport width. 2. Open the kebab ('...') menu on any row. 3. Click 'Cancel Return'. 4. Observe the screen - no confirmation is visible. 5. Inspect via devtools/automation: getBoundingClientRect() on .ant-popconfirm shows x > window.innerWidth.
Test Data: Return record #INV_20260916_04.
Expected Result: The confirmation popover renders fully within the visible viewport (AntD's collision/flip handling should reposition it), and 'Yes, cancel it' is clickable by a normal mouse user.
Actual Result: Popover computed position: x=1952.875, y=45.09, width=375.16, height=102, while window.innerWidth=1920 - entirely off-screen. Forcing a click via the element's accessibility ref (bypassing the visual position) does trigger cancellation successfully, proving the handler itself works and the defect is purely a positioning/layout regression.
Evidence: browser_evaluate getBoundingClientRect() output showing x=1952.875 against innerWidth=1920 and documentElement.scrollWidth=2328; before/after screenshots showing no visible popover despite the click registering in the DOM.
Remarks: Likely caused by the table being wider than the viewport (scrollWidth 2328 vs 1920) combined with the Popconfirm anchoring to a trigger that is itself near/past the visible right edge, with no collision-aware repositioning. Worth checking whether the same table-overflow issue affects other row-level Popconfirms/menus across the app (Inventory Record, Stock Adjust Record, Supplier List all use similar kebab-menu patterns) - not independently verified for those pages this session.

Title: Inventory Return Record summary totals ('Total Returns', 'Total Demurrage') do not exclude a Cancelled return
Description: The app's own Cancel Return confirmation text promises: 'It will be marked cancelled and left out of future totals.' After cancelling a return, the Inventory Return Record page's 'Total Returns' and 'Total Demurrage' summary cards continue to include the cancelled transaction's amounts, both immediately after cancellation and after a full page reload (ruling out a simple stale-cache/no-refetch explanation for the immediate case). This also runs counter to the general spec principle for cancellations: 'All related financial effects shall return to their previous state' (stated for Inventory Cancellation, and mirrored by this page's own promised behavior for Return cancellation).
Preconditions: Manik Pharma (598); at least one Returned transaction plus one that will be Cancelled.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Note Total Returns / Total Demurrage on /inventory-return-record with 2 active returns (e.g. Tk248 / Tk32 total across #INV_20260916_02 Tk140/Tk20 and #INV_20260916_04 Tk108/Tk12). 2. Cancel #INV_20260916_04 via its kebab menu (force-click if BUG-INV-026 blocks the visible popover). 3. Confirm its Status badge changes to 'Cancelled'. 4. Hard-reload the page. 5. Re-read the summary cards.
Test Data: #INV_20260916_04 (Tk108 return price, Tk12 demurrage) cancelled; #INV_20260916_02 (Tk140/Tk20) remains Returned.
Expected Result: After cancellation, Total Returns drops to Tk140 (1 active return) and Total Demurrage drops to Tk20.
Actual Result: Total Returns remained '(2) Tk 248' and Total Demurrage remained '(0) Tk 32' [sic - the KPI's own count label also incorrectly reads '(0)' despite a non-zero Tk32 total] both immediately after cancellation and after a full page reload, i.e. the cancelled #INV_20260916_04 is still counted in both figures.
Evidence: Before/after screenshots of the Inventory Return Record summary cards, taken pre-cancel, immediately post-cancel, and after a hard page reload - all three showing the same unchanged Tk248/Tk32 totals.
