Title: Completing an Inventory Return never credits the Pharmacy Wallet / Treasury - totalIn stays 0
Description: Spec states: 'Based on the final return amount: The amount shall be added to the Pharmacy Wallet. The Supplier Balance shall be updated accordingly.' Only the second half of this works. The supplier-balance side is correctly persisted (verified directly via the Supplier List UI: balance moved Tk0 -> Advance Tk80 immediately after completion). The Pharmacy Wallet side never happens: the Dashboard's 'Total Treasury' figure was unchanged before and after completing a Tk80 return, and the backend's own authoritative treasury report endpoint confirms this at the data layer, not just in the UI.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma (598); a batch with available quantity; a supplier to return against.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Note GET https://pms-sql-api.ems24.co/api/1.0.0/secured/reports/treasury/598?from=...&to=... (today's range) - record balance/totalIn/totalOut. 2. Complete an Inventory Return (e.g. 10 pc of TEST PRODUCT, Tk80, 0% demurrage) against a supplier. 3. Re-fetch the same treasury report endpoint and re-read the Dashboard's Total Treasury KPI.
Test Data: 10 pc return of TEST PRODUCT, Tk8.00/pc, Final Price Tk80.00, supplier Tuhin Hossain, 0% demurrage.
Expected Result: Total Treasury increases by Tk80.00, and the treasury report's totalIn for the day increases by Tk80 (attributable to the return being added to the Pharmacy Wallet).
Actual Result: Dashboard Total Treasury stayed at 'Tk -860' unchanged before and after. Raw API confirms: {"balance":-860,"totalIn":0,"totalOut":860,"groups":[{"name":"CASH","balance":-800,...},{"name":"BANK","balance":-60,...},{"name":"CARD","balance":0,...},{"name":"MFS","balance":0,...}]} - totalIn is 0 across every account for the entire day despite the Tk80 return completing successfully and correctly crediting the supplier's Advance balance in the same transaction.
Evidence: GET .../reports/treasury/598 response body showing totalIn:0/totalOut:860/balance:-860; Supplier List screenshot showing Tuhin Hossain's balance correctly at Advance Tk80 for the same transaction, proving only the wallet side is missing, not the whole transaction. Also checked Accounting > Income (Income List) after the Tk80 return: 'Total Incomes (0) / No income found' - the return credit does not appear there either, confirming the amount is not recorded in ANY financial ledger (Treasury, Income, or the Dashboard Cashbook), not merely omitted from one specific view.
Remarks: User explicitly asked whether the Pharmacy Wallet credit / 'reduce from supplier, add to pharmacy' flow had been verified after the original test pass - it had not been, and this follow-up check found it broken. This is a genuine financial-integrity gap: a pharmacy owner returning stock for a refund/credit has no way to see that money reflected anywhere in their cash position, even though the supplier's ledger correctly shows the debt. Worth checking whether the same gap affects Stock Adjustment's analogous 'Business Loss' requirement (it does - see BUG-INV-024) and whether Sale Return has the equivalent 'customer refund from wallet' requirement working correctly (not checked this session).

Title: Inventory (Default mode): empty BTP+VAT/Box shows the error 'TP per box is required' - names a field that does not exist in this mode
Feature: Add Items to Cart > Default mode > validation message
Description: In Default mode the purchase-price field is labelled 'BTP+VAT/Box' (id btpVatPerBox; there is no TP/Box field in this mode). When it is empty and the user clicks 'Add Items to Cart', the form blocks the add with the inline error 'TP per box is required'. The message uses the TP/VAT-mode wording, so it refers to a field the user cannot see. In TP/VAT mode an empty TP/Box is accepted (optional per spec section 12) and in Opening Stock mode the price is calculated from the Retail Price, so the message appears only in Default mode.
Preconditions: Manik Pharma (598); Inventory > Default mode; cart can be empty.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Inventory (Default mode). 2. Select a product that has no stored price (e.g. '3 BION'), OR select 'TEST PRODUCT' and clear the 'BTP+VAT/Box' field. 3. Enter Box Qty 2. 4. Click 'Add Items to Cart'.
Test Data: Product '3 BION' (no preloaded BTP+VAT/Box) with Box Qty 2; or 'TEST PRODUCT' with BTP+VAT/Box cleared.
Expected Result: The item is not added, and the inline error names the visible field, e.g. 'BTP+VAT per box is required'.
Actual Result: The item is not added (cart stays at its previous count), and the inline error reads 'TP per box is required'. Verified live on 2026-10-08 in both reproduction variants; the same product in TP/VAT and Opening Stock modes shows no such error.
Evidence: Playwright probe 2026-10-08: error text read from .ant-form-item-explain-error in Default mode; page text lists the field as 'BTP+VAT/Box'; TP/VAT mode with the same product added the item with no error; Opening Stock mode also added it.
Remarks: Cosmetic / wording only - the validation itself (a price is required in Default mode) is correct. Found while probing a failing cart test whose product had no stored price.

Title: Inventory (Default and Opening Stock modes, and when editing a line in Edit Inventory): a line with Box Qty 0 is accepted into the cart (0 boxes, Tk 0.00) - Box Qty must be greater than 0
Feature: Add Items to Cart > Box Qty validation (Default mode, Opening Stock mode)
Description: Box Qty must be greater than 0 (confirmed by the product owner, 2026-10-08). The form accepts 0 and adds a cart line with Box Qty 0, Total Qty 0 and Total Price Tk 0.00. Negative numbers are not affected: every numeric field clamps a typed negative to 0 (so '-1' and '-0.5' also end up as 0 and are added the same way). Only an empty or non-numeric Box Qty is blocked ('Box qty is required'). The same holds when a saved line is edited in Edit Inventory: Box Qty 0 is accepted and the line is saved with 0 boxes (confirmed live 2026-10-14).
Preconditions: Manik Pharma (598); Inventory > Default mode or Opening Stock mode; empty cart.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Inventory (Default mode). 2. Select a product (e.g. TEST PRODUCT). 3. Type 0 into Box Qty (optionally also type -1 or -0.5, which become 0). 4. Click 'Add Items to Cart'.
Test Data: TEST PRODUCT, Box Qty 0 (also reproduced with Free Qty 5), BTP+VAT/Box 33.3.
Expected Result: The item is not added; a validation message says Box Qty must be greater than 0.
Actual Result: The item is added: cart row Box Qty 0, Total Price Tk 0.00. The cart total is unchanged, and the line would flow into checkout and Complete Inventory.
Evidence: Live probe 2026-10-08 (real keyboard typing): '0' -> field 0 -> added=True, cart row {Box Qty 0, Total Price Tk 0.00}; '-1' and '-0.5' -> field clamps to 0 -> same result. Also reproduced manually by the user for '0'. Opening Stock mode re-confirmed live 2026-10-12 (retail 100, Box Qty 0 -> added, Total Tk 0.00); confirmed as a bug by the product owner for Opening Stock the same day.
Remarks: Initially mis-reported as 'negative values accepted' - that came from Playwright fill() bypassing the input's key handling; corrected the same day. Only Box Qty 0 is a real defect.

Preconditions: Manik Pharma (598); Inventory > Default mode; supplier 'jb' holds an Advance balance.
Title: Inventory (Default mode): the inventory record's Due/Status is netted against the supplier's advance - an unpaid Due & Buy record shows 'Advance Tk 0' or a reduced Due instead of its own Final - Paid
Feature: Complete Inventory > Due & Buy > Inventory Details / Inventory Record status
Description: The invoice itself is not paid (Paid < Final Price, 'Due & Buy' chosen) but its Payment Status is derived from the supplier's running balance. Because 'jb' already holds an Advance, the unpaid invoice is labelled 'Advance' with an amount of Tk 0 instead of Due/Partial, and the dialog text 'Tk X will be Due to jb. Pay later.' is not true for the supplier balance (it only reduces the advance).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Supplier has an Advance balance. 2. Add a product, go to checkout, set Total Paid = 0 (or half). 3. Complete Inventory > 'Due & Buy'. 4. Open Inventory Record / Details.
Test Data: two_plain cart, Total Paid 0 and 50% of Final Price, supplier jb (Advance Tk 842).
Expected Result: Each inventory record shows its OWN payment state: Due = Final Price - Paid - Less (e.g. bill 444, paid 222 -> 'Due Tk 222'; bill 67, paid 0 -> 'Due Tk 67'), independent of the supplier's advance. The supplier's advance/balance belongs on the Supplier List only.
Actual Result: While the supplier holds an advance the record shows a netted figure: bill 444 / paid 222 / advance 143 -> 'Due Tk 79'; bill 67 / paid 0 / advance 842 -> status 'Advance', 'Advance Tk 0'. With no advance it shows the record's own due ('Due Tk 444', 'Due Tk 75').
Evidence: logs/default_mode_live34.txt: test_payment_variants[partial-0.5], [unpaid-0.0]: "Payment Status: 'Due' not in 'Advance'".
Remarks: Confirmed as a defect by the product owner on 2026-10-11 ('keep it as a bug'). Supplier balance maths is correct in every journey (before + Final - Paid - Less). Reproduces only while the supplier holds an advance. Needs confirmation: is the status meant to be invoice-level (spec 44.1) or supplier-level? Supplier balance maths matches the workbook (M2+K4-K5-M5) in all 10 Due/Less/Advance journeys. 2026-10-11 re-run with supplier balance Tk 0: unpaid / part-paid Due & Buy shows 'Due Tk 444' / 'Due Tk 75' as expected - the 'Advance Tk 0' status only appears while the supplier still holds an advance that covers the invoice's due. 2026-10-11 later run (supplier held a smaller advance): bill 444, paid 222, Due & Buy -> record list 'Due Tk 79' (not 222): the supplier's remaining advance (143) was applied to the invoice automatically and only the rest is shown as Due. Next unpaid invoice (no advance left) -> 'Due Tk 444'. So the invoice status/due is netted against the supplier's advance; supplier balance maths is right in every case.
